Elon Musk: “The profound thing Model S showed is that an electric car can actually be the best car of any kind, period.

It broke the perception that EVs were worse than gasoline cars. If you design it right with an incredibly talented Tesla team, you can actually make an electric car better than any gasoline car.

Model S wasn’t just MotorTrend Car of the Year… I think it was the best car ever.

Then we followed it with Model X — a bit of an ambitious ‘February Egg’ of a car, maybe even an exercise in hubris. But it’s an incredible vehicle with so many small, special details most people never even notice.

At a fundamental level, Model S and Model X succeeded because they were designed with love.”

Video

Elon Musk: “This is a bittersweet moment as we hand over the last of the Model S and Model X vehicles we’ve produced.

These cars really made Tesla a great car company and changed how people saw electric vehicles.

People used to think EVs were slow, low range, undesirable… basically glorified golf carts that weren’t fun or good-looking.

It felt like you had to give up something just to be environmentally friendly.

But Model S changed that.

It proved an electric car could actually be the best car of any kind, period.”

NEWS: Elon Musk says Grok 5 will be able to “learn almost immediately, like smart humans.”

If achieved, that would represent a major leap toward AI systems that adapt and improve far more dynamically from new information and experiences.

The competition between major AI labs is already intense, and breakthroughs at this level could rapidly accelerate the entire industry.

NEWS: Tesla’s Model S and Model X continue to stand out as two of the most influential vehicles in modern automotive history.

A new “Automotive Firsts” graphic highlights how the Model S and X introduced features that later became standard across the EV industry including over-the-air updates massive center touchscreens advanced battery architecture and built-in self-driving hardware.

The Model S also helped normalize fast charging through the Supercharger network while the Model X introduced features like Falcon Wing doors and one of the lowest drag coefficients ever achieved for an SUV.

When Tesla launched these vehicles in 2012 and 2015 the auto industry looked completely different.

Today many of the software and EV design choices competitors use can be traced back to the Model S and Model X.

From the very first Tesla Model S to the very last.

One car. One decade-plus. A complete reinvention of what was possible.

The Model S didn’t follow the rules — it rewrote them. It proved an electric vehicle could be beautiful, thrilling, and practical enough to replace the gas car for real drivers. Groundbreaking range. 

Ludicrous performance. Software that evolved the car after delivery. 

It silenced the doubters and forced the entire auto industry to accelerate.
It didn’t just build hype — it electrified the world and sparked the EV revolution we’re living in today.

As this legend completes its run, we salute the car that started it all.

Thank you, Model S. You changed everything. ⚡️

Ten years ago, I walked into Tesla as an intern — January 2015, back when all we built was the Model S.

I never imagined I'd one day lead the Fremont factory where we are building some of the most amazing cars the world has ever seen.

Today we sunset the S/X program, and it's bittersweet. The first ever car I bought was a Model S. It showed me a whole new world, and a reason to believe in futuristic technology. 

The end of one thing makes room for new beginning of the other. We're letting go of something we loved a lot so we can build something even greater. Big things are already  on their way to Fremont factory— a future of amazing abundance.

Thank you, @elonmusk, for the vision. To everyone who built this with me: thank you. Onto the next chapter. 🚀
